title: Air Traffic Control in the USA

phrases.def: 控制领空的控制下空气空气空间

sentences.en: A An accident that occurred in the skies over the Grand Canyon in 1956 resulted in the establishment of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to regulate and oversee the operation of aircraft in the skies over the United States, which were becoming quite congested.
sentences.zh: 1956年在大峡谷上空的天空发生事故,导致联邦航空管理局成立,以监管和监督美国上空空中飞机的运行,因为飞机正在变得相当拥挤。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The resulting structure of air traffic control has greatly increased the safety of flight in the United States, and similar air traffic control procedures are also in place over much of the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 由此形成的空中交通管制结构大大加强了在美国的飞行安全,世界上大部分地区也制定了类似的空中交通管制程序。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: B Rudimentary air traffic control (АТС) existed well before the Grand Canyon disaster.
sentences.zh: 航空交通控制()早在大峡谷灾难发生之前就存在。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: As early as the 1920s, the earliest air traffic controllers manually guided aircraft in the vicinity of the airports, using lights and flags, while beacons and flashing lights were placed along cross-country routes to establish the earliest airways.
sentences.zh: 早在1920年代,最早的空中交通管制员就使用灯光和旗帜在机场附近手动驾驶飞机,同时在跨国家路线沿线安装信标和闪电灯,以建立最早的航道。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: However, this purely visual system was useless in bad weather, and, by the 1930s, radio communication was coming into use for АТС.
sentences.zh: 至1930年代, 无线电通讯开始用于 。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: C In the 1940s, АТС centres could and did take advantage of the newly developed radar and improved radio communication brought about by the Second World War, but the system remained rudimentary.
sentences.zh: 1940年代,中心可以而且确实利用第二次世界大战带来的新开发的雷达和更好的无线电通信,但该系统仍然很原始。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: It was only after the creation of the FAA that full-scale regulation of America’s airspace took place, and this was fortuitous, for the advent of the jet engine suddenly resulted in a large number of very fast planes, reducing pilots’ margin of error and practically demanding some set of rules to keep everyone well separated and operating safely in the air.
sentences.zh: 只有在建立美国航空局之后,美国才全面管制了领空,这是偶然的,因为喷气机的出现突然导致大量非常快的飞机,降低了飞行员的误差幅度,实际上要求制定一些规则,使所有人都能保持距离和安全地在空中运行。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: D Many people think that АТС consists of a row of controllers sitting in front of their radar screens at the nation’s airports, telling arriving and departing traffic what to do.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这包括一排在机场雷达屏幕前坐着的监控员,

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: This is a very incomplete part of the picture.
sentences.zh: 这是情况非常不完整的一部分。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The FAA realised that the airspace over the United States would at any time have many different kinds of planes, flying for many different purposes, in a variety of weather conditions, and the same kind of structure was needed to accommodate all of them.
sentences.zh: 联邦航空局认识到,美国上空的空气空间在任何时候都拥有许多不同类型的飞机,在各种天气条件下,为许多不同目的飞行,需要同样的结构来容纳所有飞机。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 分词结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: E To meet this challenge, the following elements were put into effect.
sentences.zh: 为了应付这一挑战,以下要素已经生效。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: First, АТС extends over virtually the entire United States.
sentences.zh: 首先, 几乎覆盖整个美国。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: In general, from 365m above the ground and higher, the entire country is blanketed by controlled airspace.
sentences.zh: 一般来说,从地面以上365米到更高,整个国家都设有受控领空。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: In certain areas, mainly near airports, controlled airspace extends down to 215m above the ground, and, in the immediate vicinity of an airport, all the way down to the surface.
sentences.zh: 在主要靠近机场的某些地区,受控领空从地面上向下延伸至215米,在机场附近,直达地面。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Controlled airspace is that airspace in which FAA regulations apply.
sentences.zh: 受控制的空气空间是适用航空法条例的空气空间。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: Elsewhere, in uncontrolled airspace, pilots are bound by fewer regulations.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方,在不受控制的领空,飞行员受管制较少的条例约束。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: In this way, the recreational pilot who simply wishes to go flying for a while without all the restrictions imposed by the FAA has only to stay in uncontrolled airspace, below 365m, while the pilot who does want the protection afforded by АТС can easily enter the controlled airspace.
sentences.zh: 这样,仅希望飞行一段时间而不受安哥拉武装部队所施加的所有限制的娱乐飞行员只能停留在不到365米的无控制领空,而希望得到________________________提供保护的飞行员则可以很容易地进入受控制领空。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: F The FAA then recognised two types of operating environments.
sentences.zh: 联邦联邦航空局随后承认了两种类型的经营环境。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: In good meteorological conditions, flying would be permitted under Visual Flight Rules (VFR), which suggests a strong reliance on visual cues to maintain an acceptable level of safety.
sentences.zh: 在良好的气象条件下,根据《视觉飞行规则》允许飞行,这表明要保持可接受的安全水平,就必须大力依靠视觉提示。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Poor visibility necessitated a set of Instrumental Flight Rules (IFR), under which the pilot relied on altitude and navigational information provided by the plane’s instrument panel to fly safely.
sentences.zh: 视力差需要一套仪器飞行规则,根据这些规则,飞行员依靠飞机仪器板提供的高度和导航信息安全飞行。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: On a clear day, a pilot in controlled airspace can choose a VFR or IFR flight plan, and the FAA regulations were devised in a way which accommodates both VFR and IFR operations in the same airspace.
sentences.zh: 受控空气空间的飞行员可以在明日选择VFR或IFR飞行计划,而FAA规章的设计方式既顾及VFR又顾及在同一空气空间的飞行。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: However, a pilot can only choose to fly IFR if they possess an instrument rating which is above and beyond the basic pilot’s license that must also be held.
sentences.zh: 试办人员只能选择飞航IFR, 前提是他们拥有超过基本试办执照的仪器评级,

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: G Controlled airspace is divided into several different types, designated by letters of the alphabet.
sentences.zh: G控制空域分为几种不同类型,按字母字母字母指定。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Uncontrolled airspace is designated Class F, while controlled airspace below 5,490m above sea level and not in the vicinity of an airport is Class E. All airspace above 5,490m is designated Class A. The reason for the division of Class E and Class A airspace stems from the type of planes operating in them.
sentences.zh: 无人控制领空被定为F类,而海平面5 490米以上而不是机场附近的受控领空为E类。 5 490米以上的所有领空均被指定为A类。 E类和A类领空的划分原因来自在其中运作的飞机类型。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Generally, Class E airspace is where one finds general aviation aircraft (few of which can climb above 5,490m anyway), and commercial turboprop aircraft.
sentences.zh: 一般来说,E级领空是指找到普通航空机(总之其数目可攀升5 490米以上)和商用涡轮螺旋桨飞机的地方。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: Above 5,490m is the realm of the heavy jets, since jet engines operate more efficiently at higher altitudes.
sentences.zh: 超过5,490米是重型喷气式飞机的领域,因为喷气式飞机发动机在高空更高效地运行。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: The difference between Class E and A airspace is that in Class A, all operations are IFR, and pilots must be instrument-rated, that is, skilled and licensed in aircraft instrumentation.
sentences.zh: E级和A级空气空间的区别在于,在A级,所有作业都是IFR,飞行员必须使用仪器,即飞机仪器的熟练和许可证。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: This is because АТС control of the entire space is essential.
sentences.zh: 这是因为控制整个空间是不可或缺的。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Three other types of airspace, Classes D, С and B, govern the vicinity of airports.
sentences.zh: 机场附近有另外三种类型的空气空间,即D类、Z类和B类。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: These correspond roughly to small municipal, medium-sized metropolitan and major metropolitan airports respectively, and encompass an increasingly rigorous set of regulations.
sentences.zh: 这些机场大致相当于小的市、中大都市和大都市机场,包括一套日益严格的条例。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: For example, all a VFR pilot has to do to enter Class С airspace is establish two-way radio contact with АТС.
sentences.zh: 例如,所有VFR飞行员进入类空气空间所必须做的就是与建立双向无线电联系。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: No explicit permission from АТС to enter is needed, although the pilot must continue to obey all regulations governing VFR flight.
sentences.zh: 无需获得进入该航班的明确许可,尽管飞行员必须继续遵守关于VFR飞行的所有条例。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: To enter Class В airspace, such as on approach to a major metropolitan airport, an explicit АТС clearance is required.
sentences.zh: 进入“空气空间”类,如进入主要大都会机场,需要明确的“空气空间”许可。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The private pilot who cruises without permission into this airspace risks losing their license.
sentences.zh: 未经许可巡航进入领空的私人飞行员可能会失去执照。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

items.prompt: The FAA was created as a result of the introduction of the jet engine.
Air Traffic Control started after the Grand Canyon crash in 1956
Beacons and flashing lights are still used by ATC today.
Some improvements were made in radio communication during World War II
Class F airspace is airspace which is below 365m and not near airports.
All aircraft in Class E airspace must use IFR
A pilot entering Class C airspace is flying over an average-sized city.
